row.question:
Based on the chest X-ray findings in Figure 1a and Figure 1b, which of the following is the most accurate description of the mass's location and its relationship to surrounding structures?

A) The mass is located in the right upper lung zone, adjacent to the right hilum, and obscures the right heart border.
B) The mass is situated in the right lower lung zone, merging with the right heart border, and silhouettes the right hemidiaphragm anteriorly.
C) The mass is in the left lower lung zone, obscuring the left heart border, and is separate from the diaphragm.
D) The mass is located centrally within the mediastinum, separate from the cardiac silhouette and diaphragm.
E) The mass is in the right middle lung zone, adjacent to the pleura, and is not in contact with the diaphragm.
F) The mass is located in the left upper lung zone, overlapping the left clavicle and extending to the apex.

reference.correct_choice_text: The mass is situated in the right lower lung zone, merging with the right heart border, and silhouettes the right hemidiaphragm anteriorly.

historical_prediction.json.raw_response:
Answer: B  
Reason: Figure 1a (PA chest X-ray) shows a dense opacity in the right lower lung zone that merges with the right heart border (silhouette sign), and the right hemidiaphragm is obscured anteriorly—consistent with a right lower lobe mass abutting the diaphragm and heart. Figure 1b (lateral view) confirms the mass is anterior and inferior, overlapping the diaphragm and cardiac silhouette, supporting option B.

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When mediastinal opacity obscures one heart border and tracheal deviation is present on PA CXR
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect which cardiac border is silhouetted (left border loss = left mediastinal pathology; right border loss = right-sided) and confirm tracheal deviation direction—deviation away from mass side—and compare costophrenic angle blunting severity per side.
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable if both borders obscured or in severe cardiomegaly; requires adequate inspiration and centering.

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When a well-circumscribed thoracic mass lacks acute angles at lung interface on PA CXR
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect lateral CXR for posterior location relative to cardiac silhouette and spine; obtuse angles + posterior position strongly favor extrapulmonary benign tumor (e.g., schwannoma)
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable if breast tissue or poor inspiration obscures posterior structures; does not distinguish schwannoma from other posterior neurogenic tumors
